instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each legislative agent to file a statement of expenditures with the updated registration statement.
Updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) are due by the last day of January, May, and September each year, and §101.73(D) ties expenditure statement filing times to §101.72.
Section 101.72(B) mandates filings not later than the last day of January, May, and September each year (three times per year).
The statute specifies triannual updated statements (January, May, September) rather than an annual spending report cadence.
Quarterly filing is not provided; filings are required three times per year (January, May, September).
No monthly filing requirement appears; the only periodic filing dates listed are January, May, and September.
The statute does not require semiannual reporting; it requires three updated statements per year.
The statute fixes the periodic expenditure statement filings to the triannual updated registration schedule with no alternative cadence described.
A legislative agent's statement must show the total amount of expenditures made by the legislative agent during the reporting period.

When expenditures are made for particular covered officials (and for meals over the threshold), the statement must disclose recipient name, total amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client, which itemizes expenditures by recipient/transaction.
The statute requires specific line-item details for reportable expenditures to particular officials, implying an itemized disclosure format for those expenses.
For reportable expenditures, the filer must include the specific items of legislation, if any, for which the expenditures were made.
Updated registration statements must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the covered period.
The expenditure statement requires totals and details per recipient and related legislation/client, but does not require aggregating expenditures by issue area.
Only the initial registration requires a brief description of the type of legislation, and the expenditure statement provisions do not require listing general issues.
Section 101.73 specifies totals and certain details for expenditures to covered officials but does not require reporting general subject matter categories.
The statute requires a brief description of expenditures, but it does not mandate categorization into defined expense-type categories.
Expenditures include gifts and items such as entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and §101.73 requires reporting expenditures to covered officials meeting its conditions.
The statute excludes office maintenance expenses (and employer-paid agent compensation) from 'expenditures' for employer statements, indicating indirect costs are not required to be reported.
Section 101.73 details what an expenditure statement must contain and does not require the lobbyist's name/address; those appear in registration statements under §101.72.
For reportable expenditures, the filer must disclose the identity of the client on whose behalf each expenditure was made.
The expenditure statement must provide client identity but does not require client address or other contact information.
The expenditure statement provisions do not require stating a principal's business nature; the registration statement requires a description of the type of legislation instead.
Although 'actively advocate' includes promoting or opposing legislation, §101.73 does not require reporting whether the filer supported or opposed a bill.
The expenditure statement requires disclosure of expenditures and related details but contains no requirement to report lobbying contacts.
The statute explicitly excludes compensation paid to legislative agents from the employer's 'expenditures' and does not otherwise require reporting total compensation in the spending report.

Because compensation paid to agents is excluded from reportable expenditures and no other compensation reporting requirement appears in §101.73, there is no payer-broken-down compensation disclosure requirement.
Section 101.73(A) requires each legislative agent to file a statement of expenditures with each updated registration statement, without conditioning the filing on having made expenditures.
The definition of 'expenditure' is limited to those made to or for the benefit of specified public officers/employees and does not include their household members.
